# Quick Notes
- I realized that in my loops, there were some pages that when cleaned, were left with no data. Those caused problems since they did not get a prediction generated.
- Alternatively, some pages that may have had data, may still have been dropped if none of their tokens were in the list of tokens that had a idf value calculated. 
- This messes up the analysis for nearly all of the work below. I have updated the function to recover those lost pages, but for whatever reason, it completely messes the actual accuracy of the models with PCA.
- Before realizing this issue, it did NOT seem like PCA helped with the model anyway. The model that used the TF-IDF matrix directly as input worked better. The new code accounts for this.
- All other loops with PCA are left with the old function that dropped empty/insignificant rows for archival purposes.
- The tested neural network with the updated function is at the very bottom in the section "NN without PCA"


This is just taking a look at the structure of `claims_clean`
```{r}
# original_url: url
# text_tmp: raw html
# .id: ID for an observation
# label: category label
# mclass: multiclass label
# bclass: binary label
# text_clean: processed text
claims_clean %>% head(2)
```

### Pseudocode
Take claims_clean and break into 80% training and 20% testing
Split the training into 5 folds.

For each fold:
  Take the analysis set and use a function to generate term frequencies in each document and idf values for each word. Save the idf values from the analysis set. Combine both results to get the tf-idf table (remove .id and bclass). Save the words that are in the tf-idf table
  Do PCA on the tf-idf table. Save that PCA model and the PCA values for the analysis data.
 Use that matrix of PCA values to train a neural network.
  On the assessment set, use the function to generate term frequencies in each document. With the idf values from the analysis set, generate tf-idf table for the assessment set. Ignore words that were not in training. Put those into the same analysis PCA model to get assessment PCA values.
  Put the assessment PCA values into the trained neural network and get binary predictions. 
  Calculate accuracy across folds.

### Sample NN
General structure: tokenize the data, calculate tfidf, create pca model from tfidf, calculate PCs, train the NN on the PCs
```{r}
claims_tokenized <- claims_clean %>% tokenize_fn(n = 1)
claims_tf <- claims_tokenized %>% tf_fn()
claims_idf <- claims_tf %>% idf_fn(min_doc_freq = 2, max_doc_prop = 0.90, max_terms = 1000)
tfidf_table <- tfidf_fn(claims_tf, claims_idf)

pca_model <- pca_train_fn(tfidf_table, n_pc = 50)
pca_columns <- pca_predict_fn(tfidf_table, pca_model)

claims_clean %>%
    transmute(.id, text_length = str_length(text_clean)) %>% arrange(text_length)

# Basic logistic regression like in section?
model_data <- pca_columns %>% left_join(claims_clean %>% select(.id, bclass), by = ".id")
y_vals <- model_data$bclass %>% as.numeric() - 1 # 1: relevant, 0: irrelevant
x_vals <- model_data %>% select(starts_with("PC")) %>% as.matrix()

# Model Specification
model <- keras_model_sequential(input_shape = ncol(x_vals)) %>% 
  layer_dense(1) %>% 
  layer_activation(activation = "sigmoid")

# Model Configuration
model %>% compile(
  loss = 'binary_crossentropy',
  optimizer = 'adam',
  metrics = 'binary_accuracy'
)

training <- fit(model, x = x_vals, y = y_vals, epochs = 50,
                validation_split = 0.2)
plot(training)

claims_clean %>% pull(.id) %>% length()
claims_tokenized %>% pull(.id) %>% unique() %>% length()
dim(tfidf_table)
```

# 5-fold cross validation on a basic binary classification neural network
```{r}
# Transforms cleaned text into a tfidf matrix. Transforms the tfidf matrix into principal components, and uses those to train a neural network. Generates predictions
# Stuff that can be changed: 
# length of a n-gram
# the number of ngram terms/selection criteria for the idf
# number of principal components/percentage of combined variance 
# Neural network layers/neuron numbers
# Training epochs 

set.seed(1)

# Data Split
data_split <- initial_split(claims_clean, prop = 0.8, strata = bclass)
training_data <- training(data_split)
testing_data <- testing(data_split)
folds <- vfold_cv(training_data, 5, strata = bclass)

cv_results <- vector("list", 5)

for(fold in 1:5){
  message(paste0("Fold ", fold))
  analysis_data <- analysis(folds$splits[[fold]])
  assessment_data <- assessment(folds$splits[[fold]])
  
  # Tokenize and calculate term frequency
  # Can change the length of an n-gram here
  analysis_tokens <- analysis_data %>% tokenize_fn(n = 1)
  assessment_tokens <- assessment_data %>% tokenize_fn(n = 1)
  analysis_tf <- analysis_tokens %>% tf_fn()
  assessment_tf <- assessment_tokens %>% tf_fn()
  
  # IDF from analysis
  # Can change the # of ngram terms and selection criteria
  idf <- analysis_tf %>% idf_fn(max_terms = 1000, max_doc_prop = 0.9, min_doc_freq = 2)
  
  # tfidf matrices
  analysis_tfidf <- tfidf_fn(analysis_tf, idf)
  assessment_tfidf <- tfidf_fn(assessment_tf, idf)
  
  # PCA model and PC conversion
  # Can change the number of principal components/variance proportion
  pca_model <- pca_train_fn(analysis_tfidf, n_pc = 50)
  analysis_pca_matrix <- pca_predict_fn(pca_data = pca_model, tfidf_data = analysis_tfidf)
  assessment_pca_matrix <- pca_predict_fn(pca_data = pca_model, tfidf_data = assessment_tfidf)
  
  # Consolidate data for neural network
  analysis_model_data <- analysis_pca_matrix %>% left_join(analysis_data %>% select(.id, bclass), by = ".id")
  assessment_model_data <- assessment_pca_matrix %>% left_join(assessment_data %>% select(.id, bclass), by = ".id")
  
  x_train <- analysis_model_data %>% select(starts_with("PC")) %>% as.matrix()
  y_train <- as.numeric(analysis_model_data$bclass) - 1
  
  x_assess <- assessment_model_data %>% select(starts_with("PC")) %>% as.matrix()
  y_assess <- as.numeric(assessment_model_data$bclass) - 1
  
  # Neural Network Training
  # Model Specification
  model <- keras_model_sequential(input_shape = ncol(x_train)) %>% 
    layer_dense(units = 1) %>% 
    layer_activation(activation = "sigmoid")
  # Model Configuration
  model %>% compile(loss = "binary_crossentropy",
                    optimizer = "adam",
                    metrics = "binary_accuracy")
  # Can change the number of epochs
  training <- fit(model, x = x_train, y = y_train, epochs = 50, validation_split = 0.2)

  # Generate predictions
  predictions <- predict(model, x_assess)
  probabilities <- as.numeric(predictions)
  predicted_class <- factor(if_else(probabilities >= 0.5, levels(training_data$bclass)[2], levels(training_data$bclass)[1]), 
                            levels = levels(training_data$bclass))
  
  # Metrics 
  fold_metrics <- tibble(truth = assessment_model_data$bclass, predicted = predicted_class, probability = probabilities) %>%
    summarize(accuracy = accuracy_vec(truth, predicted), 
              sensitivity = sens_vec(truth, predicted, event_level = "second"),
              specificity = spec_vec(truth, predicted, event_level = "second"),
              roc_auc = roc_auc_vec(truth, probability, event_level = "second"))

  # Store fold results
  cv_results[[fold]] <- fold_metrics
}

# Combine fold metrics
cv_results <- bind_rows(cv_results, .id = "fold")

# Calculate mean 
cv_summary <- cv_results %>%
  summarize(across(c(accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, roc_auc), mean))
```

Using unigram (word) tokens, with top 1000 IDF terms (>=2 documents, <= 90% of documents), 50 principal components, basic logistic regression model from section, 50 epochs, I get:
Accuracy: 74.1%
Sensitivity: 86.5%
Specificity: 59.8%
ROC AUC: 81.6%

Trying a neural network with 1 hidden layer, everything else the same as above.

With 1 hidden layer of 20 neurons, the metrics are:
Accuracy: 75.9%
Sensitivity: 72.4%
Specificity: 80%
ROC AUC: 83.1%

Accuracy is comparable, but specificity is now higher and closer to sensitivity level. ROC AUC also slightly increases. Notably, the accuracy seems to flatten out around 10 epochs, suggesting maybe 50 is unnecessary.

Changing to keeping PCAs that explain a combined 80% of variance results in the following:

Accuracy: 77.9%
Sensitivity: 76.6%
Specificity: 79.5%
ROC AUC: 84.5%

Accuracy and ROC AUC slightly increasing. Sensitivity and Specificity don't seem to be improving. Seems like ~130 PCs. 

- Idea of 2/3 rule? (2/3 # of neurons in hidden layer). Changing the number of neurons in the hidden layer didn't have a significant difference. (Adding more neurons isn't improving?)
- Try adding a second hidden layer of the same size? Also no significant difference

# NN without PCA
Try feeding the tf-idf matrix as input directly:

```{r}
# TESTING NN WITHOUT USING PCA

set_random_seed(1)
# Data Split
data_split <- initial_split(claims_clean, prop = 0.8, strata = bclass)
training_data <- training(data_split)
testing_data <- testing(data_split)
folds <- vfold_cv(training_data, 5, strata = bclass)

cv_results <- vector("list", 5)

for(fold in 1:5){
  message(paste0("Fold ", fold))
  analysis_data <- analysis(folds$splits[[fold]])
  assessment_data <- assessment(folds$splits[[fold]])
  
  # Tokenize and calculate term frequency
  # Can change the length of an n-gram here
  analysis_tokens <- analysis_data %>% tokenize_fn(n = 1)
  assessment_tokens <- assessment_data %>% tokenize_fn(n = 1)
  analysis_tf <- analysis_tokens %>% tf_fn()
  assessment_tf <- assessment_tokens %>% tf_fn()
  
  # IDF from analysis
  # Can change the # of ngram terms and selection criteria
  idf <- analysis_tf %>% idf_fn(max_terms = 7500, max_doc_prop = 0.9, min_doc_freq = 2)
  
  # tfidf matrices
  analysis_tfidf <- tfidf_fn_updated(analysis_tf, idf, all_ids = analysis_data)
  assessment_tfidf <- tfidf_fn_updated(assessment_tf, idf, all_ids = assessment_data)
  
  # Consolidate data for neural network
  analysis_model_data <- analysis_tfidf %>% left_join(analysis_data %>% select(.id, bclass), by = ".id")
  assessment_model_data <- assessment_tfidf %>% left_join(assessment_data %>% select(.id, bclass), by = ".id")
  
  x_train <- analysis_model_data %>% select(-.id, -bclass) %>% as.matrix()
  y_train <- as.numeric(analysis_model_data$bclass) - 1
  
  x_assess <- assessment_model_data %>% select(-.id, -bclass) %>% as.matrix()
  y_assess <- as.numeric(assessment_model_data$bclass) - 1
  
  # Neural Network Training
  # Model Specification
  model <- keras_model_sequential(input_shape = ncol(x_train)) %>% 
    layer_dense(units = 20, activation = "relu", kernel_regularizer = regularizer_l2(0.001)) %>% 
    layer_dense(units = 20, activation = "relu", kernel_regularizer = regularizer_l2(0.001)) %>% 
    layer_dense(units = 1) %>% 
    layer_activation(activation = "sigmoid")
  # Model Configuration
  model %>% compile(loss = "binary_crossentropy",
                    optimizer = "adam",
                    metrics = "binary_accuracy")
  # Can change the number of epochs
  early_stop <- callback_early_stopping(monitor = "val_loss", patience = 10, restore_best_weights = TRUE)
  training <- fit(model, x = x_train, y = y_train, epochs = 20, validation_split = 0.2, callbacks = list(early_stop))

  # Generate predictions
  predictions <- predict(model, x_assess)
  probabilities <- as.numeric(predictions)
  predicted_class <- factor(if_else(probabilities >= 0.5, levels(training_data$bclass)[2], levels(training_data$bclass)[1]), 
                            levels = levels(training_data$bclass))
  
  # Metrics 
  fold_metrics <- tibble(truth = assessment_model_data$bclass, predicted = predicted_class, probability = probabilities) %>%
    summarize(accuracy = accuracy_vec(truth, predicted), 
              sensitivity = sens_vec(truth, predicted, event_level = "second"),
              specificity = spec_vec(truth, predicted, event_level = "second"),
              roc_auc = roc_auc_vec(truth, probability, event_level = "second"))

  # Store fold results
  cv_results[[fold]] <- fold_metrics
}

# Combine fold metrics
cv_results <- bind_rows(cv_results, .id = "fold")

# Calculate mean 
cv_summary <- cv_results %>%
  summarize(across(c(accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, roc_auc), mean))

cv_summary

dim(x_assess)
length(y_assess)
dim(assessment_data)
```
7500 tokens (1-grams), some regularization (0.001) at each step, 20 neurons each in 2 hidden layers
Accuracy: 80.2%
Sensitivity: 76.9%
Specificity: 83.8%
ROC AUC: 86.8%

Tried playing around with the # of tokens, the size of n-grams, some regularization, removing a hidden layer, changing # of neurons in each layer. This was what I found worked best.


# Applying to testing set
```{r}
set_random_seed(1)
# Tokenize and calculate term frequency
training_tokens <- training_data %>% tokenize_fn(n = 1)
training_tf <- training_tokens %>% tf_fn()

# IDF from training
idf <- training_tf %>% idf_fn(max_terms = 7500, max_doc_prop = 0.9, min_doc_freq = 2)

# tfidf matrix
training_tfidf <- tfidf_fn_updated(training_tf, idf, all_ids = training_data)

training_model_data <- training_tfidf %>% left_join(training_data %>% select(.id, bclass), by = ".id")
x_train <- training_model_data %>% select(-.id, -bclass) %>% as.matrix()
y_train <- as.numeric(training_model_data$bclass) - 1


# Neural Network Training
# Model Specification
model <- keras_model_sequential(input_shape = ncol(x_train)) %>% 
  layer_dense(units = 20, activation = "relu", kernel_regularizer = regularizer_l2(0.001)) %>% 
  layer_dense(units = 20, activation = "relu", kernel_regularizer = regularizer_l2(0.001)) %>% 
  layer_dense(units = 1) %>% 
  layer_activation(activation = "sigmoid")
# Model Configuration
model %>% compile(loss = "binary_crossentropy", 
                  optimizer = "adam",
                  metrics = "binary_accuracy")
# Can change the number of epochs
early_stop <- callback_early_stopping(monitor = "val_loss", patience = 10, restore_best_weights = TRUE)
model_training_history <- fit(model, x = x_train, y = y_train, epochs = 20, validation_split = 0.2, callbacks = list(early_stop))


# Break testing data
testing_tokens <- testing_data %>% tokenize_fn(n = 1)
testing_tf <- testing_tokens %>% tf_fn()
testing_tfidf <- tfidf_fn_updated(testing_tf, idf, testing_data)
testing_model_data <- testing_tfidf %>% left_join(testing_data %>% select(.id, bclass), by = ".id")
x_test <- testing_model_data %>% select(-.id, -bclass) %>% as.matrix()
y_test <- as.numeric(testing_model_data$bclass) - 1

# Generate predictions
predictions <- predict(model, x_test)
probabilities <- as.numeric(predictions)
predicted_class <- factor(if_else(probabilities >= 0.5, levels(testing_data$bclass)[2], levels(testing_data$bclass)[1]), 
                          levels = levels(testing_data$bclass)) 

# Metrics
test_metrics <- tibble(truth = testing_model_data$bclass, predicted = predicted_class, probability = probabilities) %>%
  summarize(accuracy = accuracy_vec(truth, predicted),
            sensitivity = sens_vec(truth, predicted, event_level = "second"),
            specificity = spec_vec(truth, predicted, event_level = "second"),
            roc_auc = roc_auc_vec(truth, probability, event_level = "second")
  )
confusion_matrix <- conf_mat(tibble(truth = testing_model_data$bclass, estimate = predicted_class), truth, estimate)

test_metrics
confusion_matrix 
```

Testing Metrics:
Accuracy: 83.6%
Sensitivity: 83.5%
Specificity: 83.8%
ROC AUC: 89.0%

- Uses only the 7500 most common tokens when calculating the IDF.
- Neural network has 2 hidden layers with 20 neurons each, ReLU activation, and ridge regularization with alpha = 0.001. Adam optimizer, binary cross entropy loss function. Trained for 20 epochs with a 10 epoch early stop if no progress.

# Train on all data
```{r}
set_random_seed(1)
training_data <- claims_clean
class_levels <- levels(training_data$bclass)

# Tokenize all observations
training_tokens <- training_data %>% tokenize_fn(n = 1)

# Calculate term frequencies
training_tf <- training_tokens %>% tf_fn()

# Calculate IDF using all available observations
idf <- training_tf %>%
  idf_fn(max_terms = 7500, max_doc_prop = 0.9, min_doc_freq = 2)

# Generate TF-IDF matrix
training_tfidf <- tfidf_fn_updated(training_tf, idf, all_ids = training_data)

training_model_data <- training_tfidf %>% left_join(training_data %>% select(.id, bclass), by = ".id")

x_train <- training_model_data %>%
  select(-.id, -bclass) %>%
  as.matrix()

y_train <- as.numeric(training_model_data$bclass) - 1


# Neural Network
model <- keras_model_sequential(input_shape = ncol(x_train)) %>%
  layer_dense(units = 20, activation = "relu", kernel_regularizer = regularizer_l2(0.001)) %>%
  layer_dense(units = 20, activation = "relu", kernel_regularizer = regularizer_l2(0.001)) %>%
  layer_dense(units = 1) %>%
  layer_activation(activation = "sigmoid")

# Configuration

model %>% compile(loss = "binary_crossentropy", optimizer = "adam", metrics = "binary_accuracy")

# Train
model_training_history <- fit(model, x = x_train, y = y_train, epochs = 20)
```

```{r}
save_model_tf(model, "results/binary_nn", overwrite = T)
save(idf, class_levels, file = "binary_idf_levels.rda")
```
